findings.prior_defect: Reproduced against the FROZEN v1.16 bundle at a03923cd4b09e8e11d40e8cf13819f8df763063a before anything was changed, in four parts. (1) The exact value at EVIDENCE-SET-WORKFLOW.json#toctou.law contains the bare derive_attachment_state (DIAGNOSTIC / NON_AUTHORIZING in the canonical map), the verb 'refuses', and no diagnostic marking anywhere in the value itself. (2) AUTHORITY-FUNCTION-CLASSES.json#authorizing_slots contains exactly ten hand-written key paths and not this one. (3) The v1.16 validator source literally contains the marker string 'no longer' in its context list and splits clauses only at '. ' and '; ', so the clause the scanner examined was the whole sentence, which contains 'no longer' - the suppression is mechanical and provable from the frozen source. (4) With comma-aware, paren-aware clause splitting the same sentence isolates the clause 'and derive_attachment_state refuses' (DIAGNOSTIC / NON_AUTHORIZING), which as written carries no class token, so the defect is caught immediately. The executable authority was never wrong: no runtime dispatch reads a function name from any artifact, so this is a consumer-facing frozen-authority defect, which is why it blocks merge without being a runtime bypass.
findings.correction: Three parts, no runtime change. (1) EVIDENCE-SET-WORKFLOW.json#toctou.law now names the AUTHORIZING refusal - tools/authority_lib.py#derive_attachment_state_authorizing, with #derive_attachment_state_for_session as the equivalent session wrapper loading through #load_governed_evidence_set - and names the bare-evidence function explicitly AS DIAGNOSTIC / NON_AUTHORIZING in its own clause, for fixtures and diagnosis only. TOCTOU SEMANTICS ARE UNCHANGED: the same record-id/content-digest law and the same two additional seals, asserted equal to the parent's. (2) The hand-written authorizing_slots and diagnostic_slots dictionaries are REMOVED from AUTHORITY-FUNCTION-CLASSES.json and replaced by a frozen SEMANTIC slot_discovery_law: a slot is authorizing if its value designates a function as authoritative, deciding, refusing, enforcing, deriving current authority state, gating eligibility or commit, or validating - whatever its key is called - and the inventory itself is GENERATED into the new AUTHORITY-SLOT-INVENTORY.json by validate_v1_17.py through the new tooling module tools/authority_slots.py, one row per reference with artifact, key path or line, referenced function, authority role, canonical class and current/historical status. 32 authorizing slots are discovered across 54 current artifacts where v1.16 hand-listed ten. (3) The scanner is rebuilt around two fail-closed laws - R1 every reference to a demoted function in a current artifact carries an explicit class token in its OWN clause; R2 every clause that designates authority names a function of class authorizing - with clause boundaries at '.', ';', ':', ',' and newline at parenthesis depth zero and only before whitespace (so an argument list, a dotted module path and a version number stay intact), wrapped markdown rejoined into logical lines first, an explicit signal precedence (class or history token in the clause, then structured key path, then that clause's authority verbs), NO bare negation in any token list, module-aware normalization of six reference forms to one canonical (module, name), and an artifact scope DERIVED from precedence status plus a published document role (NORMATIVE_AUTHORITY, CORRECTION_RECORD, GENERATED_EVIDENCE, HISTORICAL_INPUT) rather than a filename pattern.
